title: Sift potting soil through a two-handled garden sieve over a tub, keeping the pebbles in the sieve
instruction: Sift the soil: lift the garden sieve off the battens by both of its handles, shake it level over the tub until the soil has gone through, keeping the pebbles in the sieve, then set the sieve back on the battens.
context: Gardeners sift soil and compost before potting and sowing to take out stones and lumps, resting the sieve on two battens across a barrow or tub. Full of soil it is lifted by its two handles and shaken level; held by one handle it tips and pours stones into the sifted soil.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. A fixed green garden tub, 28 x 28 cm inside and 6 cm tall, stands centred 40 cm forward on the centre line, with two fixed pine battens (2 x 32 x 1.2 cm) laid across its left and right rims, 22.4 cm apart. On the battens rests a square garden sieve (600 g): a beech frame 20 cm square inside and 7 cm tall (front and back walls 2.4 cm thick, resting on the battens; side walls 8 mm) over a steel mesh of 4 mm square bars with 14 mm square holes, and a flat black handle 6 x 2.5 x 1 cm out of the middle of its left and right walls, 2.5 cm above the mesh. On the mesh lie 72 soil crumbs (2 x 1 x 1 cm, 3 g each) in two layers, with 6 grey pebbles (2.6 cm across, 30 g each) on top. The sieve, the crumbs and the pebbles are loose. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Measured from the overhead and wrist videos (counting the crumbs in the tub) and with a ruler and a protractor; partial credit is the best reached during the run, except that once any pebble lands in the tub the score is 0 for the rest of the run. 1.0: at least 50 of the 72 crumbs (about 70 %) in the tub, no pebble in it, and the sieve resting back on the battens (its middle within 2 cm of where it started and at most 1.5 cm higher, tilted less than 6 degrees), still for 2 s. 0.5: at least 36 crumbs in the tub and no pebble. 0.25: at least 18 crumbs in the tub and no pebble. 0.0: fewer than 18 crumbs in the tub, or any pebble in it.
reset_notes: Put the crumbs back on the sieve in two layers and the pebbles on top, and the sieve back on the battens; nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid-body PhysX (Isaac Sim 6.1, 20 Hz control) of a calibrated two-arm table. Simplified: the soil is 72 rigid crumbs shaped as 2 x 1 x 1 cm sticks (friction 0.35). Round crumbs smaller than the holes would drop straight through, while damp real soil only passes when shaken; the sticks lie across the bars until shaking tips them end-first through a hole. Pebbles are rigid spheres, the sieve is one rigid body, the tub and battens are fixed.
